newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stockmarket soars to historic high.
newsitem.headline: French stockmarket soars to historic high.

text.p: French stocks soared to a historic high on Monday after Wall Street's latest record encouraged European investors to break the laggard bourse's previous record set in February 1994.

The blue chip CAC-40 index surged at the opening to surpass the previous record of 2,360.98 points in the first few minutes of trading. The index was 1.71 percent higher at 2,367.27 points at 1140 GMT after edging back from a high of 2,370.87.

"The bourse is swept up by Wall Street, by the bond markets and by expectations of higher corporate results in France for 1997," said Jean-Pierre Filbien, director of sales at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Paris.
The U.S. Dow Jones industrial average set its fourth closing record of the new year last Friday after reversing an early drop to close 78 points higher at 6,703.67.
German shares also climbed to record levels on Monday.

Christian Mariais, a portfolio manager at Paris brokerage Oddo, said the Dow's latest feat reassurred investors who had feared that Wall Street's bull run would end just as the French bourse came up to speed.

"The U.S. market is rising because U.S. company profits are higher. The outlook for earnings in 1997 is good, so there may be a correction on Wall Street, but we're not expecting a crash," Mariais said.
Although the French economy is growing very slowly, the rise in the dollar, low French interest rates and corporate restructurings are expected to boost company profits this year.
Mariais estimated the bourse would advance at the same pace as last year, when the CAC-40 index rose 23.71 percent.
Its price-earnings ratio is 20 times estimated 1996 earnings and 16.5 times estimated 1997 earnings.

Until late last year, the bourse sat out the rally sweeping the U.S. and European bourses to new records. But most analysts and strategists say the French market is upward bound, at least for the first half of 1997.
"The gainers may not be the same issues. The advance this year may favour cyclical shares, but for the index, the increase should be about the same," Mariais said.
Among the top gainers on the CAC, luxury goods group LVMH rose 2.3 percent to 1,440 francs after announcing on Saturday that it had closed the purchase of duty free chain DFS.

Renault shares surged 3.6 percent to 112.40 francs. Chairman Louis Schweitzer said in an interview in the newspaper Figaro that he expected the car operation to show a bigger loss in 1996 but aimed for breakeven in 1997. The stock was also helped by reports of the huge popularity of the new Megane Scenic car.
Shares in Carrefour, the star of the retail sector, were three percent higher at 3,388 francs.
Pierre Amancic, deputy director of IFF Bourse, said the bourse had risen so fast that it risked an abrupt correction.
"The indicators are signalling that the market's overbought. There's a risk of a violent retracement that could take us back as far as 2,200 points," he said.
But in the medium to long term, he said he expected the bourse to rise further, helped by a recovery in the long-suffering financial sector.
Analysts and fund managers surveyed recently by Reuters expect the CAC to rise to at least 2,450 points this year.

Daniel Dourmat, portfolio manager at Caisse Centrale des Banques Populaires, said he also expected the market to pull back to digest its gains before resuming an advance toward 2,400-2,450 points by summer.
His main concern is the fragility of the Tokyo market, which could spread to others if Japanese investors are obliged to sell assets abroad to cover losses at home.
Brokers said the bourse will face a test on Tuesday when market-moving U.S. inflation figures are issued at 1330 GMT.
